text: The transfer step calls the rwb-partner issueInstruction activity as a Temporal child call, answers the case move as the stage outcome the parent CaseWorkflow applies, writes the transfer record as the asset_sale rows of the pool with their listing references, takes the committee approval as the P7 ApprovalWorkflow answer, reads the R-DIS-59 timer specification from the rule row in force, and leaves PRT-06 to the partner portal surface of rwb-partner.
why: No source gives the element names of the partner call or of the case move, a transfer table, the pool or approval columns, the approval shape, a timer value or the owner of PRT-06, and the step cannot be built, faked or tested without a reading of them.
read: Architecture v5 slide 19 OUT names the partner activity and the approval child and gives the service only AssetTakenOn and AssetSold; the Ownership Map gives asset_sale, listing and (by the slide 19 and 41 and TSD T3.1 reading) asset to S5, approval and rule_row to P7, partner_instruction to S9 and template to P6; TSD S5 T3.1 gives asset_sale the sale columns and no pool, price-version or approval column; R-DIS-60 closes the transfer from RAMC_TRANSFER_PENDING and belongs to the completing step.
confirm: Solution architect with the owners of rwb-partner, rwb-case, rwb-decision and rwb-comms
impact: The step builds on Day 1 against the fakes; the partner, case and approval names and the missing transfer table are confirmed before SIT, and the map is corrected if the reading is not accepted

text: The legacy endpoints of RWB-E4-031 are kept in the story as named operations of their owners and not as operations of this step: the valuation path is rwb-valuation's and the listing path is the pricing story's, and this step provides only the two asset reads.
why: The legacy Endpoints and Permission checks tables name two POST operations with right C while the transfer of a pool calls neither, and TSD S5 T-A.1 gives the two reads right R, so the legacy rows cannot be read as this step's own surface.
read: Ownership Map api rows POST /assets/{assetId}/valuations owner S1 under the ruling ASM-A6-api-6 and POST /assets/{assetId}/listings owner S5 with the ruling ASM-A6-api-15; TSD S5 T-A.1 rows API-S5-001 and API-S5-002 with right R and API-S5-003 to API-S5-005 with rights C and U.
impact: No C right is granted to this step, and the two POST operations are built by their owning stories without change here

text: No requirement id is claimed for this slice: the story traces to FEAT-AST-22, to FSD S5 A2.22 and to legacy RWB-E4-031 until a requirement row exists for the feature.
why: The split plan and the legacy index carry empty reqs lists and TSD S5 T8 names no requirement row for FEAT-AST-22, so any id written here would be invented.
read: split_plan.json slice RWB-S5-E4031-APP with reqs as an empty list; legacy_index.json RWB-E4-031 with reqs as an empty list; TSD S5 v2 T8 rows REQ-S5-001 to REQ-S5-010 mapped to FEAT-AST-01 and FEAT-AST-08.
confirm: Business analyst and the program requirements owner
impact: Traceability runs to the feature and its metric until the requirement row is added at the next requirements version

text: The contract declares the pool reference, the transfer-price template version and the approval reference as identifiers with the placeholder, declares the four consumed rows with their placeholders, declares no REST approval operation and publishes no event for the step.
why: TSD S5 T3.1 has no column for the three references, no source publishes the consumed operation and element names or an approval operation, and Architecture v5 slide 19 OUT gives the service only AssetTakenOn and AssetSold, so the baseline can only fix the names it has and mark the rest.
read: Ownership Map rows and Architecture v5 slides 19, 41 and 43; TSD S5 T3.1 DF-SAL-001 to DF-SAL-019; TSD S5 T-A.1; FSD S5 A2.22 field catalog; Temporal and Drools Design slide 13 for the ApprovalWorkflow on rwb-decision.
confirm: Solution architect with the owners of rwb-partner, rwb-case, rwb-decision and rwb-source-data
impact: The baseline can be tagged on Day 1 and every placeholder is replaced when the owners confirm its name

text: The instruction is declared as the Temporal activity issueInstruction on the partner task queue, and the partner REST paths of the Ownership Map are recorded as rwb-partner's own surface that rwb-asset never calls.
why: Architecture v5 slide 19 OUT names the Temporal activity, the Temporal and Drools Design puts every cross-service stage call on the owner's queue with its answer in history, and the Ownership Map publishes partner paths without saying who calls them, so one call type has to be chosen and the other explained.
read: Ownership Map api rows POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions, GET /partner/instructions and the two POST /partner/instructions rows with owner S9; Architecture v5 slide 19 IN and OUT and its TMP tag; Temporal and Drools Design slides 13, 14 and 27.
confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-partner owner
impact: The baseline declares one call path and a drift test refuses a partner path on the rwb-asset document
